versions.how_we_got_here:
New Zealand uses a proportional voting system (MMP), so one party rarely wins outright and governments are built through coalition deals. Christopher Luxon has been prime minister since late 2023, leading a coalition of National, ACT and NZ First.

The election held this weekend produced no clear winner, and the BBC describes a gloomy, tired electorate delivering the tightest result in years.

players.name: Christopher Luxon (PM, caretaker)
players.wants: To stay in office by rebuilding a governing majority; he leads a caretaker government during the talks.

players.name: The opposition bloc
players.wants: To show it can assemble a majority of its own and take power.

players.name: Smaller parties
players.wants: Policy wins and ministries in return for their votes; they hold the leverage while the count is close.

versions.stakes: Weeks of uncertainty over who runs Australia's closest neighbour, and what that means for budget, trade and security decisions in the Pacific. Markets rarely move much on New Zealand politics, but the NZ dollar can wobble on a long stalemate.
versions.current_state: As of 9 November: no clear winner. Luxon says talks will take about three weeks and he will lead a caretaker government meanwhile. Nikkei Asia calls the result knife-edge.
versions.watch_next:
- Which small parties hold the balance of seats once counting settles.
- Whether any bloc announces a coalition deal inside the three-week window.
- Any change in New Zealand's line on China, Australia or the Pacific.

timeline.event: Luxon is sworn in as prime minister of a National–ACT–NZ First coalition.
Election result shows no clear winner; Luxon announces roughly three weeks of coalition talks.
Caretaker government in place while parties negotiate.
